name: retro-asm
description: Plain-English tooltips, colours and jump-around navigation for retro assembly: TMS9900 (TI-99/4A, xas99), 6502 (Commodore 64, KickAssembler; BBC Micro, BeebAsm) and Z80 (ZX Spectrum, sjasmplus). Other chips are added as data files.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In a folder you have not trusted, tooltips, colours, links and navigation still work. Build, run and chip files from the project folder are switched off until you trust it.

retroAsm.defaultDialect.description: The chip to assume when a file extension isn't matched to one.

retroAsm.dialectByExtension.markdownDescription: Which chip to use for which file extension, for example `{ ".asm": "z80" }`. The *Switch chip* command fills this in for you.

retroAsm.dialectFolders.markdownDescription: Folders holding your own chip files (`*.json`). A plain name is looked for inside the open project folder; a full path is used as it is. A chip file with the same `id` as a built-in one replaces it.

retroAsm.checks.description: Underline likely mistakes: misspelt instructions, the wrong number of operands, labels that don't exist, labels defined twice.

retroAsm.hoverInComments.description: Show a tooltip (and allow jumping) when a label name is mentioned inside a comment.

retroAsm.routineSummaries.description: Show a summary line above each routine: who calls it, where it sits in memory and how big it is, and which registers it changes.

retroAsm.showAddresses.description: Show each line's memory address down the left of the code. Ctrl+Alt+A switches it on and off.

retroAsm.loadAddress.markdownDescription: Where the program is loaded in memory, in hex, for code that doesn't say so itself with `AORG`. Leave empty to use the chip's usual place (`A000` for a TI-99/4A program loaded with Editor/Assembler).

enumDescriptions: Draw a block of bytes as a picture when its name or comments say it is one (PAT_..., sprite, drawing...).
Draw every block of bytes as a picture.
retroAsm.pictures.description: Show BYTE and DATA blocks as pictures in tooltips.

retroAsm.original.skoolFile.markdownDescription: The SkoolKit disassembly (`.skool` file) of the original game you are porting. Addresses such as `$A420` in your comments then open it at that address, and their tooltip shows the code there. A full path, a path from the project folder, or a folder holding the file. Leave empty to look for a `.skool` file in the source's folder (and two folders inside it), then in the folder above.

retroAsm.build.command.markdownDescription: The command that builds your program. Leave empty to work it out: a `build.bat` (or `build.sh`) next to the source is used if there is one, otherwise xas99 is run directly. You can use `${file}`, `${fileDirname}`, `${fileBasename}`, `${fileBasenameNoExtension}`, `${name}` (the TI file name) and `${workspaceFolder}`.

retroAsm.build.runCommand.markdownDescription: The command that starts your emulator after a good build. Leave empty to look for `classic99\\classic99.exe` near the source (Windows).

retroAsm.build.xas99Path.description: Full path to xas99.py, if it isn't in an xdt99 folder near your source.

retroAsm.build.python.description: The command that runs Python. Leave empty for 'python' on Windows and 'python3' elsewhere.

retroAsm.build.askFirst.markdownDescription: Ask before running a build script, assembler or emulator that comes from the project (a `build.bat` near the source, a tool found in its folders, or a command in its own settings). Each command is asked about once per folder. Only your own user settings can switch this off.

viewsWelcome.contents: Open an assembly file (.a99, .asm, .6502, .z80 ...) to see its chip, size, warnings and routines here.
The screen, sound, keyboard and ROM addresses your code uses will be listed here.
